title: Read guidance names shell readers and line ranges
summary: The read tool's guidance names `cat`, `sed`, `head` and `tail` as the shell commands it replaces and says `offset` and `limit` read a line range, restoring wording that an unrelated revert had removed.
firstReason: The note records a benchmark run in which this sentence was the only change, and a session that read ranges with `sed` 60 times. Tool guidance is model-facing text and carries over word for word.

title: Present declares workspace source files
summary: The `present` tool declares existing workspace files as deliverables by path and optional description, without reading or copying them. The UI opens the current file in the host's default application; a moved or deleted file makes the declaration unavailable.
firstReason: Declaring instead of copying avoids a second store and a second place to edit. It is a small host-side rule.

title: Apply patch file editing
summary: `apply_patch` accepts one Codex-style patch that adds, updates, deletes and moves several files. A pure library parses and matches it, the filesystem service gains `patchText`, `deleteFile` and `moveFile` with intent events and version guards, and a whole-patch preflight commits nothing if any part is refused.
firstReason: Multi-file edits in one guarded call are cheaper for the model and keep mutation intents visible for review. Preflight before commit, and the stated outcome of a half-finished move (`sourceDeleted`), are the failure semantics to keep.

title: Shipped filesystem mutation defaults
summary: The `apply_patch` file-editing tool is on by default in the base profiles, and the read-before-write guard (the filesystem observation policy, which refuses a write to a file the model has not read or that changed since the read) ships switched off; a deployment turns it back on with one setting.
firstReason: These are shipped defaults chosen from benchmark runs, not a JavaScript mechanism. The Go default configuration should start from the same defaults and keep the guard as an optional component; the filesystem-tools area confirms the values.
